messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: oncall@redwood - REDIS CLOUD ALERT: managed-cache connectivity errors detected in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 clusters. Error rate spike affecting auth-cache and rate-limiter reads. Please acknowledge.

alyssa: acked. i'm oncall. seeing 500s from auth validation and a ton of 429 spikes reported from our api gateway.

mike: seeing the same, dashboard shows cache miss rate up to 95% for auth:key:* and latencies 300-800ms to rediscloud endpoints.

sandra: customer reports rolling in to support: multiple small apps seeing login failures and high latency. Is there an immediate mitigation?

alyssa: first steps: 1) confirm scope, 2) flip rate-limiter to local mode, 3) enable auth-token fallback to K/V in memory for short TTLs, 4) message customers and update status page.

kevin: customer comms draft (short): "We're investigating authentication timeouts and rate limiting errors caused by a third-party cache provider. We're mitigating with temporary local fallbacks and will update." OK to post? :thinking_face:

alyssa: yes post that. mike can you run the override to local ratelimit? I have the handoff to infra for the cache fallback.

mike: running override now.

mike: ```
# switch rate-limiter to local in-memory mode for 15m
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/admin/ratelimit/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"mode":"local","expire_seconds":900}'
```

mike: override accepted by control plane, rate-limiter telemetry now showing traffic on local token buckets. gateway 429s dropping by ~70% in last 60s.

alyssa: great. next, auth-cache fallback: moving to local LRU cache with very short TTLs to avoid revalidating against provider. sandra, can you coordinate changes in prod config?

sandra: rolling out a feature-flag flip to enable local auth cache for all regions. deploying canary to one LB. patch: ```
PATCH /services/auth/config
{
  "auth_cache": "local_fallback",
  "local_ttl_seconds": 30
}
```

sandra: canary looks good for 5 minutes, no increased error rate. rolling to remaining LB nodes.

alyssa: monitoring logs for downstream effects. noticed spikes in oauth-provider errors when retries increased. We should also reduce aggressive retries for auth to avoid cascading failures. mike can you throttle retry policy?

mike: changed retry policy in gateway: max_retries=1, backoff=200ms.

rediscloud-support-bot: Update from RedisCloud: "We've identified a networking issue in our peering layer affecting multiple clusters. Our engineering team is applying mitigations; customer impact may persist 30-90 minutes. Status: incident#RC-11234. We will update every 15 minutes." (https://status.rediscloud.example/RC-11234)

kevin: posted initial customer message to status.redwood.ai and sent an email to top 50 customers with high RPS. Copy: "We mitigated immediate effects by switching to local fallbacks and limiting retries. We're monitoring and will provide updates."

alyssa: handoff: i'm going offline in 20m for meeting, mike will take primary. mike you have ownership of the incident timeline and vendor comms. i'll stay available for questions.

mike: taking handoff. current impact: auth validation errors ~5% of requests globally, rate-limiter 429s reduced to baseline but still slightly above normal in eu-west-1. Mitigations applied: rate-limiter local mode, auth local cache TTL=30s, retry policy reduced.

mike: quick diagnostics log sample:
```
ERROR auth_cache.go:142 fetchRedis: dial tcp 10.23.45.67:6379: i/o timeout
WARN ratelimiter.go:87 remote: read timeout, falling back to local bucket
INFO gateway.go:421 auth-fallback=local ttl=30
```

rediscloud-support-bot: Update: "We've applied a route fix in our peering fabric for eu-west-1. We're seeing partial recovery; some connections still fail. Next update in 10 minutes."

kevin: customer impact note for SRE incident report: "Partial authentication failures and elevated latency for auth-protected endpoints. A subset of customers saw login failures and 429s. Mitigation: local rate-limiter and auth cache fallbacks. Vendor: RedisCloud networking incident RC-11234."

mike: planning next steps: 1) keep local fallbacks until vendor confirms full recovery + 30m, 2) re-evaluate TTL after recovery, 3) run cleanup job to warm auth-caches gradually to avoid thundering herd. Any objections?

alyssa: SGTM. also add an alert to disable local-fallback automatically once vendor reports full recovery for 30m to avoid drift.

sandra: scheduling the cleanup job now, will stagger keys with Jitter=5s.

rediscloud-support-bot: Update: "Recovery progressing; error rates dropping. We're monitoring. We will close incident once peering is stable for 30 consecutive minutes."

mike: posting final interim update to status: "We've applied local fallbacks; service functionality is largely restored. Root cause is a third-party networking degradation with our managed cache provider. We'll return to normal ops after provider confirms stability."
